title: Joins without surprise row counts
objectives: Join two tables on their key
Spot a key that isn't unique before it doubles your rows
Choose between JOIN and LEFT JOIN when a row has no match

exercises.prompt: List every order once, with its customer's name and amount, in order_id order. Keep order 105, whose customer is missing.
hints: Run the starter and count the rows. There are 5 orders. How many rows come back, and which are missing or doubled?
Customer 2 is in customers twice, and customer 4 isn't there at all.
LEFT JOIN to (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, name FROM customers) keeps every order exactly once.
